description: Solo team by Sherdil Khan, participating virtually from Lahore, Pakistan in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Working on the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge — storytelling about NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.
summary: Three rovers still stand on the Moon. A robot lies silent on Mars. Why did nobody bring them back? This is the story of the machines NASA left behind — the Lunar Rover, the Opportunity rover, and the InSight lander — what they did, what science they made possible, and why some of them are still working today. Told in a 30-second video with photos, voiceover and subtitles, so any school student can follow it.
details: The project is a 30-second video telling the story of the machines NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars: the three Lunar Roving Vehicles (Apollo 15, 16 and 17), which together travelled 90.4 km; the Opportunity rover, planned for 90 sols, which worked for 5,111 sols and travelled 45.16 km; and the InSight lander, which detected more than 1,300 marsquakes, including the largest, magnitude 5, on 4 May 2022, before retiring in December 2022. The video uses photos, voiceover and subtitles, so any school student can follow it. It explains what each machine did, what science it made possible, and why some of them are still working today. The video is the project deliverable: a story told in 30 seconds or less, made to be understood by any school student. SI disclosure: the five still images in the video were AI-generated, the voiceover is AI text-to-speech, and the script and subtitles were written and edited with the help of an AI assistant. All facts were verified against NASA mission records in the NSSDCA Archive.
